harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Restored tickets.sql into PostgreSQL database helpdesk, repaired automatic ID allocation, preserved the source export and imported records, and verified persistence through a node1 reboot.
actions_performed: Installed CentOS 5-compatible PostgreSQL 8.1.23 without changing the OS release or kernel
Advanced tickets_id_seq beyond the imported maximum
Verified implicit inserts received unique IDs 101 and 102, then rolled back the probe records
Restarted node1 safely and verified PostgreSQL, data, sequence state, and source export recovered

evidence.requirement: Restore the export while preserving existing ticket IDs and text
evidence.summary: Restore succeeded; after reboot the database contained exactly IDs 1, 2, and 100 with their original subjects.

evidence.requirement: Repair automatic ID allocation above the imported maximum
evidence.summary: The stale sequence was observed at 1, repaired to 100, and two implicit inserts received unique IDs 101 and 102.
tickets.sql remained under /srv/legacy2/postgresql-sequence-repair with unchanged SHA-256 5a9b51de0c539f9ffedd0ca1424be6549bbef62a5414b6545d879d9c1be973c5.

evidence.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use compatible software
evidence.summary: CentOS 5.11 and kernel 2.6.18-398.el5 remained unchanged; PostgreSQL 8.1.23 from the CentOS 5 archive was used.

Healthy baseline boot ID 935518f3-c010-4e53-8000-000000000000 was captured, reboot acknowledged, new boot ID 9329589e-d38f-415e-8000-000000000000 observed, and PostgreSQL plus all ticket data, sequence state, and source file recovered.
